anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the TPS2121RUXR (U5) symbol's right-hand column lists only three pins: OUT on pin 1 (to the VBUS net / TP1), ST on pin 8 (wired to GND), and GND on pin 12. Pin 9 does not appear on the symbol at all, and pin 8 is not connected to OUT/VBUS.
anomalies.expected: The specification states for U5: 'OUT (pins 1/1_1/8/8_1) ... onto the VBUS net' and 'ST(pin9)/GND(pin12) go to GND'. That is, physical pad 8 must be an OUT pin (tied to VBUS) and pad 9 must be the ST pin (tied to GND).

evidence.quote: Power sheet, U5 (TPS2121RUXR) right column: 'OUT 1' to VBUS arrow/TP1, 'ST 8' to GND, 'GND 12' to GND; left column 7,6,5,2,4,3,11,10; no pin 9 drawn
a common OUT (pins 1/1_1/8/8_1) feeding the board's unregulated VBUS rail ... ST(pin9)/GND(pin12) go to GND

anomalies.impact: On the footprint, pad 8 of the TPS2121RUXR is an OUT pin (internally bonded to pad 1). Wiring symbol pin 8 to the ST/GND net therefore shorts the mux output (VBUS) to ground, so the buck converter U8 never receives input and the 3.3 V rail (and the whole board) stays dead; the real status pin (pad 9) is left floating.

parsed.summary: Most of the build matches the specification (SPI/CS GPIO mapping, heater-switch wiring, power-mux input/output nets, buck feedback, TVS/diode placements, and all readable passive values), but the U5 TPS2121RUXR symbol's pin numbering deviates from the intended design: ST is shown on pin 8 (to GND) with pin 9 absent, whereas the spec requires OUT on pin 8 and ST on pin 9, which would short the mux output to ground on the assembled board.
